messages:
Maria G.: Quick Q — can I attach redacted request logs to the PS Jira? Logs contain user emails and a hashed user_id field. I plan to remove emails and blank Authorization headers, but keep hashed ids. Is that OK, and should the ticket be labeled 'Internal' or 'Confidential'? Also PS engineers may need to download the file.
Ana (Security): Short answer: don't include direct PII or auth tokens. Hashed IDs can still be re-identifiable if unsalted or tied to other data — treat them as personal data unless you apply irreversible salted hashing and separate salt storage. If PS is an external vendor, mark as Confidential and get a DPA + sec approval. If it's internal-only and you have removed emails/IPs/tokens, 'Internal' can be OK, but prefer 'Confidential' when in doubt.
Ana (Security): Recommended workflow:
1) remove Authorization/Set-Cookie headers
2) redact emails via regex
3) replace IPs with <REDACTED_IP>
4) apply one-way salted hash to user_id (store salt in Secrets Manager, not in the ticket)
Example redaction command:
```
sed -E 's/(Authorization:).*/\1 REDACTED/' logs.json | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/<REDACTED_EMAIL>/g' > logs.redacted.json
```
Upload guidance: put the redacted file in a secure bucket (eg s3://redwood-secure/jira-attachments/<TICKET>) with ACL = team-only, add metadata tag `data-classification:confidential`, then paste the bucket link in the Jira. Do not attach raw logs directly to Jira or public Confluence.
Josh L.: Quick follow-up — if we do salted hash, where should the salt live? Can we keep it referenced in the ticket so PS can reproduce mappings?
Ana (Security): Don't store the salt in the ticket body. Store secrets in the secrets manager/KMS and reference the secret id in the ticket if necessary. If PS needs mapping access, prefer generating an anonymized repro dataset with synthetic IDs or request a temporary, scoped credential via the security request flow. For any vendor access open a security request at https://redwood.internal/sec-requests with justification and list of emails that need access.
Maria G.: Got it — I'll run the redaction steps, upload to the secure bucket, mark the Jira as Confidential, and open a sec request if PS needs download access. Thanks! :thumbsup:
sec-bot: automated reminder — Files that may contain PII must be stored only in approved secure buckets. See data classification policy: https://redwood.internal/policies/data-classification
